blocks.text: 26. Automation
blocks.raw_html: 26. Automation

blocks.text: When working with a Set, you may want to adjust device or mixer controls to change the character of the sound over time. While you can always tweak parameters manually, in some situations it might be more effective for the tweaks to happen automatically, especially if you want to ensure that parameter changes occur at specific points in time on subsequent playbacks. Automation allows you to save a record of the adjustments made to specific parameters over time.

blocks.text: Any control whose value automatically changes in the course of the playback is automated. Practically all mixer and device controls in Live can be automated, including the song tempo. A colored LED that appears next to a parameter indicates that the parameter has been automated. The LED is typically red, though the exact color depends on the theme you are using. Note that blue LEDs always indicate modulated rather than automated parameters.

blocks.text: 26.1 Recording Automation in Session View
blocks.raw_html: 26.1 Recording Automation in Session View

blocks.text: You can record automation in the Session View in two ways: by recording it in Session clips or by recording the Session into the Arrangement. If you choose the latter, any changes to parameters made in Session View will be recorded as track-based automation in the Arrangement’s automation lanes rather than clip-based automation in the Session clips. Recording automation into the Arrangement View also allows you to automate the tempo directly from the Session View.

blocks.text: Then, arm the tracks in whose clips you want to record automation. To record automation in all tracks, set the Record Session automation in option in Live’s Record, Warp & Launch Settings to All Tracks.

blocks.text: 26.3 Overwriting Automation
blocks.raw_html: 26.3 Overwriting Automation

blocks.text: If there is existing automation in a clip or a track’s automation lane, it will be overwritten if you make new adjustments to the same parameter while recording. For example, if you recorded automation for a parameter in a looping clip on first playback, any additional changes you make to the parameter when the loop restarts will be recorded and replace the original changes.

For example, if you recorded automation for a parameter in a looping clip on first playback, any additional changes you make to the parameter when the loop restarts will be recorded and replace the original changes.

blocks.text: In the Session View, how the automation gets overwritten depends on how you adjust a parameter while recording. When using the mouse, the parameter returns to the previously recorded value as soon as you release the mouse. This is referred to in some applications as “touch” behavior. When using knobs or faders on MIDI controllers, the parameter holds the last set value until the end of the clip or its loop, which is known as “latch” behavior in some applications. Note that when recording automation in a Session clip for the first time, Live uses the “latch” behavior, regardless of the adjustment method.

blocks.text: 26.5 Viewing Automation
blocks.raw_html: 26.5 Viewing Automation

blocks.text: Automation envelopes contain a series of breakpoints that represent a given parameter’s values across the timeline. The envelopes are displayed on top of the clip’s or track’s content, which can be helpful when lining up breakpoints with the audio waveform or MIDI notes. An automation envelope’s vertical axis represents the parameter value and the horizontal axis represents time.

blocks.text: While you can record automation, you can also use the Envelope Editor or automation lanes to create new automation envelopes by adding individual breakpoints with the mouse or keyboard, by drawing the envelopes with Draw Mode enabled, or by inserting automation shapes.

blocks.text: 26.6.1 Adding Automation Envelope Breakpoints
blocks.raw_html: 26.6.1 Adding Automation Envelope Breakpoints

blocks.text: You can draw a new automation envelope for a parameter by inserting breakpoints with the mouse or keyboard in the Envelope Editor or an automation lane. To insert a breakpoint with the mouse, make sure the parameter you want to automate is selected in the chooser, then click anywhere on the dashed line. Inserting a breakpoint creates an automation envelope, which is reflected by the dashed line changing into a solid line. You can also click and drag on the line to set a desired value for the breakpoint before inserting. Hold Shift as you drag to make finer adjustments to the parameter value. Double-clicking anywhere outside of the line creates a new breakpoint at that location.

You can also create new breakpoints at an exact value by hovering over the line to view the value, then right-clicking and choosing the Add Value option.

blocks.text: One very creative use of clip envelopes is to modulate the sample offset. Sample offset modulation makes the most sense for rhythmical samples, and is only available for clips that are set up to run in the Beats Warp Mode.

blocks.text: Imagine the audio is read out by a tape head, the position of which is modulated by the envelope. The higher a value the envelope delivers, the farther away the tape head is from its center position. Positive envelope values move the head towards the “future,“ negative values move it towards the “past.“ Fortunately, Live performs the modulation in beats rather than centimeters: A vertical grid line is worth a sixteenth note of offset and the modulation can reach from plus eight sixteenths to minus eight sixteenths.

blocks.text: 27.3 Mixer and Device Clip Envelopes
blocks.raw_html: 27.3 Mixer and Device Clip Envelopes

blocks.text: Clip envelopes can be used to automate or modulate mixer and device controls. Since mixer and device controls can potentially be controlled by both types of envelopes at the same time (and also by the Arrangement’s automation envelopes), this is a potential source of confusion. However, modulation envelopes differ from automation envelopes in one important way: Whereas automation envelopes define the absolute value of a control at any given point in time, modulation envelopes can only influence this defined value. This difference allows the two types of envelopes to work together in harmony when controlling the same parameter. To help you distinguish between these, automation envelopes are colored in red, whereas modulation envelopes are colored in blue. Additionally, in parameters with knob controls, automation moves the absolute position (or the “needle”), whereas modulation is indicated by the blue segment on the ring.

blocks.text: Imagine that you have recorded volume automation for an audio clip so that it gradually fades out over four bars. What happens to your fade-out when you create a modulation envelope that gradually increases the mixer volume over four bars? At first, your fade-out will become a crescendo, as the modulation envelope gradually increases the volume within the range allowed by the automation envelope. But, once the decreasing automated value meets with the increasing modulation envelope value, the fade-out will begin, as automation forces the absolute control value (and the operable range of the modulation envelope) down.

blocks.text: 27.3.2 Modulating Pan
blocks.raw_html: 27.3.2 Modulating Pan

blocks.text: The Pan modulation envelope affects the mixer pan stage in a relative way: The pan knob’s position determines the intensity of the modulation. With the pan knob set to the center position, modulation by the clip envelope can reach from hard left to hard right; the modulation amount is automatically reduced as you move the pan knob towards the left or right. When the pan knob is turned all the way to the left, for instance, the pan modulation clip envelope has no effect at all.

blocks.text: 27.5.3 Imposing Rhythm Patterns onto Samples

blocks.text: So far, we have been talking about imposing long envelopes onto small loops. You can also think of interesting applications that work the other way around. You can certainly think of other parameters that such a pattern could modulate in interesting ways.

owner_requirements.title: Automation and modulation indicators
owner_requirements.contract: An automated control has a theme-dependent colored indicator, typically red; blue denotes modulation. Session automation is available as a clip envelope, while Arrangement automation is displayed in track lanes.

owner_requirements.title: Session automation recording eligibility
owner_requirements.contract: Session clip automation recording uses Automation Arm, eligible armed tracks and Session Record. Record Session automation in: All Tracks permits recording into all playing Session clips regardless of track arm, including automation overdub without recording MIDI notes.

owner_requirements.title: Session recording stop controls
owner_requirements.contract: Session Record can stop automation recording while playback continues; Stop ends transport and recording. Recorded clip automation is viewed/edited in the Envelope Editor.

owner_requirements.title: Session transfer and performance recording
owner_requirements.contract: Session-to-Arrangement recording stores parameter changes as track automation, not Session clip automation, and can record tempo changes. Copying automated Session clips to Arrangement also copies automation as track automation; Session performance recording includes existing clip automation alongside live parameter changes.

owner_requirements.title: Arrangement automation recording
owner_requirements.contract: With Automation Arm enabled, Arrangement automation recording applies to all tracks. Arrangement Record is described as starting transport/recording by default and records tempo, mixer and device adjustments into track lanes; this is no unconditional transport-start guarantee.

owner_requirements.title: Arrangement recording stop controls
owner_requirements.contract: Arrangement Record can stop recording while playback continues; the adjacent Stop button ends both transport and recording.

owner_requirements.title: Overwrite and Session touch/latch contexts
owner_requirements.contract: Adjusting an already automated parameter during recording replaces its recorded adjustments. For Session overwrite, mouse release returns to prior automation, whereas MIDI knobs/faders hold the new setting until clip/loop end. A first Session automation pass uses the hold behavior regardless of input method. No overwrite interval or controller protocol law is supplied.

owner_requirements.title: Manual override presentation
owner_requirements.contract: With recording off, manually changing an automated parameter overrides its automation, turns its automation indicator gray and activates Re-Enable Automation. This is distinct from overwriting recorded data.

owner_requirements.title: Global and per-parameter re-enable
owner_requirements.contract: The Control Bar Re-Enable Automation button restores all overridden automation; a parameter context-menu command restores only that parameter. The active button indicates at least one overridden automated parameter.

owner_requirements.title: Session relaunch re-enable role
owner_requirements.contract: Relaunching a Session clip that contains automation is another documented way to re-enable overridden automation. This does not identify every affected target, launch boundary or Arrangement-return transition.

owner_requirements.title: Session envelope selection
owner_requirements.contract: The Session Envelope Editor Automation toggle and Device/Control choosers select a target envelope; device/mixer and MIDI Ctrl entries are described. Automated controls/devices have indicators; an unautomated selected control appears as a dashed line at its current value. Actual entries depend on clip type.

owner_requirements.title: Session adjusted-envelope filter
owner_requirements.contract: Show Adjusted Envelopes Only combines Session Device/Control choices into an Automated Control chooser; Show All Envelopes restores the full choices. An unautomated envelope already displayed remains displayed when filtering is enabled.

owner_requirements.title: Stacked Session control focus
owner_requirements.contract: With Envelope Editor open and Clip/Device Views stacked, clicking a track device or mixer control displays its envelope, including unautomated controls. Adjusted-only filtering prevents newly opening an unautomated envelope this way.

owner_requirements.title: Arrangement Automation Mode and choosers
owner_requirements.contract: Automation Mode button or A opens main track automation lanes. Device/Automation Control select envelopes; None hides the envelope and empties the control chooser. Automated entries have indicators and an untouched selected parameter is dashed.

owner_requirements.title: Arrangement filters and focus commands
owner_requirements.contract: Show Automated Parameters Only combines the Arrangement choosers; Show All Parameters restores them. In Automation Mode, clicking a control or its Show Automation/Show Automation in New Lane commands selects its envelope. With automated-only filtering, untouched controls cannot newly open and those menu options are disabled/unavailable; an already displayed untouched envelope remains.

owner_requirements.title: Add lane and main-lane None
owner_requirements.contract: Add Automation Lane moves the main envelope into an additional lane and sets main Device to None. Selecting a new main target permits another lane; Add is absent while None is selected.

owner_requirements.title: Additional lane visibility and order
owner_requirements.contract: A main-lane toggle hides/shows additional lanes; when main Device is None, hiding promotes the top additional lane to main. Additional lanes can be reordered by drag; arrows navigate lanes or show/hide from main context.

owner_requirements.title: Existing lane focus and duplicate limit
owner_requirements.contract: Choosing a parameter already in an additional lane focuses that lane. Ctrl-click Windows/Option-click macOS on Add creates a duplicate of the main envelope, with up to two such duplicates documented.

owner_requirements.title: All lanes and lane removal
owner_requirements.contract: Alt Windows/Cmd macOS Add or Add Lane for Each Automated Envelope adds lanes for automated parameters. Remove applies to selected additional lanes; modified Remove also removes lanes below. Main-lane Add and additional-lane Remove are available in the corresponding header menus.

owner_requirements.title: Breakpoint insertion
owner_requirements.contract: Clicking a selected control’s dashed envelope line inserts a breakpoint and makes it solid. Click-drag sets the new point value, Shift refines the adjustment, and double-click away from the line inserts there. Hover values and Add Value context entry support a chosen displayed value.

owner_requirements.title: Breakpoint grid and display
owner_requirements.contract: Inserted/moved breakpoints snap to grid, with Alt Windows/Cmd macOS bypass. Hover/drag exposes point values; segment hover/drag shows the closest breakpoint’s value. Shift horizontal drag constrains the horizontal axis and Shift vertical drag refines value adjustment.

owner_requirements.title: Discrete envelope presentation
owner_requirements.contract: Discrete controls such as toggles/radio choices display stepped rather than diagonal automation and permit only the square inserted shape.

owner_requirements.title: Draw Mode and snapping
owner_requirements.contract: Draw Mode is toggled through Options, Control Bar or B; holding B temporarily enables it when off. Drawing creates grid-width steps by default; grid size and Snap to Grid or Alt Windows/Cmd macOS bypass alter drawing alignment.

owner_requirements.title: Shape insertion extent
owner_requirements.contract: Context-menu automation shapes can be inserted at a marker or time selection; selection width determines horizontal extent and parameter range the vertical extent, while no selection uses current grid width. Source text names sine, triangle, sawtooth, inverse sawtooth, square, ramps and ADSR.

owner_requirements.title: Waveform and ramp surroundings
owner_requirements.contract: Inserted waveforms retain their shape irrespective of surrounding values, whereas ramps depend on values on either side of the insertion selection. Exact ramp coefficients, clipping and boundary events are unknown.

owner_requirements.title: Breakpoint deletion and selection
owner_requirements.contract: Points can be dragged; clicking a breakpoint deletes it and joins its neighbors by a new segment. Background drag selects multiple points, whose point drag moves the selection and whose context Delete removes selected points.

owner_requirements.title: Segment movement and selection edges
owner_requirements.contract: Dragging near a segment moves it; Shift-click/hold then releasing Shift is an alternative selection gesture. Moving a segment inside a time selection inserts points at the edges, and moving it outside inserts further edge points. Fine vertical and constrained horizontal drags are documented.

owner_requirements.title: Drop overwrites and drag preview
owner_requirements.contract: Dropping a dragged point/segment onto existing breakpoints overwrites them; while dragging before drop, existing parts are not permanently overwritten. This says nothing about Escape rollback or transaction atomicity.

owner_requirements.title: Diagonal curve gesture
owner_requirements.contract: Alt Windows/Option macOS segment drag adds a curve only to diagonal segments; modified double-click changes curved to straight. Numeric curve controls and runtime interpolation remain with the finite envelope/mix owners.

owner_requirements.title: Exact value editing
owner_requirements.contract: Edit Value on a point/segment accepts a typed value. With multiple selected points, the edited point takes that value and the others move relatively. Admission, saturation and error grammar are unknown.

owner_requirements.title: Stretch and skew handles
owner_requirements.contract: Time-selection handles transform the selected envelope: top/bottom centers stretch vertically, side centers horizontally and corners skew. Outline snaps with horizontal bypass; Shift refines vertical stretch and Alt Windows/Option macOS mirrors opposite handles. Dragging over outside points removes them.

owner_requirements.title: Simplify Envelope command
owner_requirements.contract: Simplify Envelope on a selected segment reduces unnecessary breakpoints using straight/curved segments. The source supplies no error tolerance, optimum algorithm or guaranteed reduction for every input.

owner_requirements.title: Delete Automation parameter action
owner_requirements.contract: Parameter Delete Automation context action or Ctrl-Backspace Windows/Cmd-Delete macOS deletes that parameter’s automation, removes its indicator and returns the value to its default. This does not identify a numeric default or general clip-editor shortcut dispatch.

owner_requirements.title: Clear command scopes
owner_requirements.contract: Clear Envelope removes selected-parameter envelope; lane-header Clear All Envelopes of… removes automated envelopes for the selected device; Clear All Envelopes removes automation throughout the Set. Partial removal uses point/segment editing instead.

owner_requirements.title: Tempo envelope and mapped range
owner_requirements.contract: Tempo can be recorded during Arrangement recording or edited in Main’s Mixer/Song Tempo lane. Tempo Minimum/Maximum Range controls set its displayed BPM range and also the value range of a MIDI controller assigned to tempo. Numeric mapping, global tempo precedence and clock response remain separate.

owner_requirements.title: Lock Envelopes entry point
owner_requirements.contract: Lock Envelopes is available through its toggle or Options menu. Arrangement REQ-ARRANGEMENT-032 retains the lock-on clip-move contract; the source’s broader lock-off move statement does not close that owner’s partial-selection and transformation unknowns.

owner_requirements.title: Envelope Edit commands and target transfer
owner_requirements.contract: Cut, Copy, Duplicate and Delete on an automation-lane time selection affect only selected envelope portions rather than clip content or other portions; multi-lane selections apply to the included envelopes. Segments can be copied across time and parameter targets, without a conversion rule for unrelated controls.

owner_requirements.title: Clip-type chooser vocabulary
owner_requirements.contract: Clip Envelopes tab has Device and Control choosers; audio clips expose Clip sample controls, track effects and mixer, while MIDI clips expose MIDI Ctrl, track devices and mixer. Altered envelopes have adjacent indicators and an adjusted-only filter.

owner_requirements.title: Session versus Arrangement envelope kinds
owner_requirements.contract: Session clips offer Automation/Modulation toggles; Arrangement Clip View exposes modulation only and track automation uses lanes. Automation specifies a control’s absolute value while modulation influences its current/automated value. Both kinds can coexist, with separate indicators and knob position/ring presentation; no universal combiner formula follows.

owner_requirements.title: Clear clip envelope entry
owner_requirements.contract: Clear Envelope in the Clip View envelope context menu resets the selected clip envelope to its default. Exact default values and the source’s shortcut-to-menu wording remain unresolved; parameter Delete Automation is a distinct context.

owner_requirements.title: MIDI Envelope Auto-Reset option
owner_requirements.contract: MIDI Envelope Auto-Reset is offered through Options or the Sample Editor context menu and is described as resetting certain MIDI control messages at new clip start. Which messages/values, delivery time and persistence are unknown.

owner_requirements.title: Non-destructive sample modulation
owner_requirements.contract: Clip-envelope modulation is non-destructive to the referenced sample on disk; clips can reuse one sample with different envelopes. Render/resample/consolidate are separate ways to commit audio, owned by their workflow pages.

owner_requirements.title: Audio transposition envelope context
owner_requirements.contract: The audio Clip/Transposition workflow uses Warp on and supports Draw Mode or fine breakpoint edits. owner_requirements.title: Audio Clip Gain modulation role
owner_requirements.contract: Clip/Gain envelope can shape sample level. Its influence is relative to Clip Gain, can attenuate to silence and cannot exceed that absolute setting; this documentary role supplies no calibrated gain-domain formula.

owner_requirements.title: Sample Offset eligibility
owner_requirements.contract: Clip/Sample Offset modulation is available only in Beats Warp Mode and is edited as a clip envelope. The chapter’s beat-scrambling examples do not establish random, resampling or analytic cut-and-splice behavior.

owner_requirements.title: Track volume stage and indicator
owner_requirements.contract: Clip Gain and Track Volume are distinct envelope targets; Track Volume modulation affects the mixer’s post-effect gain stage and a dot below its slider indicates the modulated setting. No stored-unit or signal multiplier law is restated.

owner_requirements.title: Send modulation ceiling role
owner_requirements.contract: Send modulation is relative to the Send control: it cannot open the send beyond the knob and can reduce it to minus infinity. This does not extend finite send coefficients or define event conversion.

owner_requirements.title: Pan modulation contextual range
owner_requirements.contract: Pan modulation range depends on the base knob: center permits the full stereo span, movement toward an edge reduces available influence, and full left is described as no-effect. This is not a pan law or formula for every mode.

owner_requirements.title: Device modulation relative role
owner_requirements.contract: Clip modulation acts on devices in that clip’s track and changes controls relative to their current setting rather than defining preset values. Per-device eligible targets and combination arithmetic require their owners/evidence.

owner_requirements.title: MIDI controller envelope editing
owner_requirements.contract: MIDI Ctrl/Control selects listed controller envelopes for creation/editing with steps or points, including imported/recorded data indicated by adjacent LEDs. Most controller numbers through 119 are described as supported; this is not every number or a MIDI codec. Receiver conventions may differ from names such as Pitch Bend or Pan.

owner_requirements.title: Envelope-local region controls
owner_requirements.contract: Unlinking gives the selected envelope its own local region/loop controls and colored loop braces. Its Loop switch is independent of the sample’s Loop switch, allowing a one-shot envelope while the sample continues looping.

owner_requirements.title: Independent envelope lengths and start markers
owner_requirements.contract: Each unlinked envelope can have its own loop length, extended by braces or numeric controls, including non-bar-aligned lengths. Its start marker identifies where envelope playback begins on clip start; start/end and braces obey the zoom-adaptive grid. No clip-time equation or sample-rounded extent follows.

owner_requirements.title: Local-loop rhythmic role
owner_requirements.contract: Local envelope loops may be shorter or longer than source playback and can be shaped with handles/shapes. The source describes tempo-relative repetition and grid-hidden independent endpoints; it does not specify clock arithmetic, rate limits or a free-running oscillator implementation.

owner_requirements.title: Linked envelope Warp interaction
owner_requirements.contract: In Linked mode, moving a clip Warp Marker lengthens/shortens its envelope accordingly, and Warp Markers can be adjusted within the envelope editor. Exact marker/envelope transformation and interpolation stay unknown or with the finite Warp owner.

assessments.quote: When working with a Set, you may want to adjust device or mixer controls to change the character of the sound over time. While you can always tweak parameters manually, in some situations it might be more effective for the tweaks to happen automatically, especially if you want to ensure that parameter changes occur at specific points in time on subsequent playbacks. Automation allows you to save a record of the adjustments made to specific parameters over time.

assessments.quote: Any control whose value automatically changes in the course of the playback is automated. Practically all mixer and device controls in Live can be automated, including the song tempo. A colored LED that appears next to a parameter indicates that the parameter has been automated. assessments.quote: Clip envelopes can be used to automate or modulate mixer and device controls. Since mixer and device controls can potentially be controlled by both types of envelopes at the same time (and also by the Arrangement’s automation envelopes), this is a potential source of confusion. quotes.quote: Note that the warp settings determine how accurately Live’s time-warping engine tracks the envelope shape. To obtain a more immediate response, reduce the Grain Size value in Tones or Texture Mode, or choose a smaller value for the Granulation Resolution in Beats Mode.

Imagine the audio is read out by a tape head, the position of which is modulated by the envelope. The higher a value the envelope delivers, the farther away the tape head is from its center position. Positive envelope values move the head towards the “future,“ negative values move it towards the “past.“ Fortunately, Live performs the modulation in beats rather than centimeters: A vertical grid line is worth a sixteenth note of offset and the modulation can reach from plus eight sixteenths to minus eight sixteenths.

Some sample offset envelope gestures have a characteristic effect: a downward “escalator“ shape, for instance, effectively repeats the step at the envelope’s beginning. Similarly, a smooth ramp with a downwards slope is slowing time and can create nice slurring effects when the slope is not quite exactly 45 degrees; try this with a 1/32 Granulation Resolution.

Imagine that you have recorded volume automation for an audio clip so that it gradually fades out over four bars. What happens to your fade-out when you create a modulation envelope that gradually increases the mixer volume over four bars? At first, your fade-out will become a crescendo, as the modulation envelope gradually increases the volume within the range allowed by the automation envelope. But, once the decreasing automated value meets with the increasing modulation envelope value, the fade-out will begin, as automation forces the absolute control value (and the operable range of the modulation envelope) down.
Now, as you play the clip, you can hear the one-bar loop fading out over eight bars.

If you are into sound synthesis, you may want to think of a clip envelope with a local loop as an LFO. This LFO is running in sync with the project tempo, but it is also possible to set up a loop period odd enough to render the envelope unsynchronized. By hiding the grid, you can adjust the clip envelope loop start and end points independently of a meter grid.
